# read_B — pp. 30–32 (leaves n31–n33), established from the images

Line counts: p. 30 five lines, p. 31 five lines (leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, with the usual gap before the second ༔),
p. 32 five lines. The witness's line breaks match the print on all three pages (15/15 lines).
Crops: each line in thirds at ×3, doubtful syllables at ×5–×12 (scratchpad `B/`).

## The image overruled the witness (14)

| page.line | witness → print | why |
|---|---|---|
| 30.1 | འཁྱམས་དགུས་བྱུང → འཁྱམས་དགོས་བྱུང | the vowel over ག is the V-shaped naro of this print (same as on ནོ in the same line), and there is no zhabs-kyu under ག; the other recension also has དགོས |
| 30.1 | (line end) བདག་གིས་ངོ → བདག་གྶི་ངོ | line-end abbreviation: gigu over ག and a small ས hung under it (ག + U+0FB6 + ི), as at 20.4 in read_A. Kept as printed; needs `# fix: གྶི => གིས` |
| 30.2 | (line end) འདི་ནས་ནི་ → འདི་ནས་ནི | no tsheg: the gigu runs into the frame and the space between ན and the frame at head height is empty (checked pixel by pixel). Needs `# fix: ནིའགྲོ => ནི་འགྲོ` |
| 30.3 | ཆགས་པ་དང་ཞིན་པ → ཆགས་པ་དང་ཞེན་པ | straight e-stroke rising to the left (as on ཚེ just before), not a gigu loop; the same word at the end of the line is also ཞེན |
| 31.2 | ཀུན་ལ་དངངས་སྐྲག → ཀུན་ལ་དངངྶ་སྐྲག | only three letter columns: ད, ང, and a ང with a small ས hung under it (U+0FB6). Checked at ×10. The same form returns at 32.2. Kept as printed; needs `# fix: དངངྶ => དངངས` |
| 31.4 | (line end) ངོ་འཕྲོད་པའི་ → ངོ་འཕྲོད་པའི | no tsheg between the gigu of འི and the frame (pixel check). Needs `# fix: པའིགནད => པའི་གནད` |
| 32.1 | གསལ་ལ་འཚོར་བ → གསལ་ལ་འཚེར་བ | there is a separate stroke above ཚ that rises to the left (a drengbu), as well as the letter's own tick, and no naro; the other recension also has འཚེར |
| 32.1 | འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ་༔ → འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔ | ༔ comes straight after ངོ with no tsheg (×8) |
| 32.1 | (line end) མ་འཇིགས་ → མ་འཇིགས | ས touches the frame and there is no tsheg. Needs `# fix: འཇིགསཤིག => འཇིགས་ཤིག` |
| 32.2 | མ་དངངས་ཤིག → མ་དངངྶ་ཤིག | three columns, with ས under the second ང, the same form as 31.2. At 32.4 the same word is written in full in four columns (དངངས), which shows that the reduced form is real and not a reading error. Needs `# fix: དངངྶ => དངངས` (the same fix line covers both places) |
| 32.2 | དེ་ནི་ཀྱོད་རང → དེ་ནི་ཁྱོད་རང | the base is ཁ (vertical left stroke and loop), not the cross of ཀ |
| 32.3 | རི་རི་འོད་ངོ་༔ → རི་རི་འོང་ངོ༔ | the two letters after འོ are the same shape, and the second one is the ང of ངོ, so the first is ང too. A tsheg separates them, and ༔ follows ངོ with no tsheg. The other recension has འོང་ངོ |
| 32.3 | ཁྱོད་རང་གྱི་ཆོས → ཁྱོད་རང་གི་ཆོས | there is no ya-btags under ག: only the long stem (×10). The other recension also has རང་གི |

(There are 13 rows and 14 changes, because row 32.3 འོང་ངོ༔ holds two of them: the letter and the tsheg. Listed by syllable: དགོས, གྶི,
ནི (tsheg), ཞེན, དངངྶ, པའི (tsheg), འཚེར, ངོ༔, འཇིགས (tsheg), དངངྶ, ཁྱོད, འོང, ངོ༔, གི.)

## [?] (1)

- 31.2 ངོ[?]་ཤེས་བྱ: the space above ང is filled by the subscripts and descenders of line 31.1, so a naro cannot be
  seen apart from them. The e-stroke right after it belongs to ཤེ. Candidates: ངོ་ཤེས (taken; the witness reading and the
  set phrase, used again at 32.2 as ངོ་ཤེས་པར་གྱིས) or ང་ཤེས (no sense).

## Things checked that the image does not decide (witness kept, no [?])

- པ and བ cannot be told apart reliably at this scan resolution: both show as a closed triangle once the head-line
  and tsheg merge. The witness is followed in every case: 30.1 སྤྲད་བ, 31.1 འཕྲོད་པའི (the print's habit
  འཕྲོད་བ would lead one to expect བ here; at ×8 the letter looks like a closed box, but the བ of བར་དོ and the
  certain པ of ཡིན་པར look the same), 31.4 སྣང་པ, 31.4 ངེས་པར, 31.4 འཕྲོད་པའི.
- ད and ང look nearly alike in this cutting. 31.3 སྐད་ངག is kept as the witness has it.
- 32.3 (line end) རང་སྒྲ་: a small dot sits between the top of ས and the frame. It is taken as the tsheg the witness has.
- Filler dots (··· after the last syllable) at 30.3 ཀྱང, 30.4 གྱིས, 30.5 ལ, 31.2 པར: the first dot is written
  as the tsheg, as in the witness, and the rest are left out (as in read_A).
- 30.5 ཇི་ལྟར་ཤར: after ལྟར there is a tsheg with a speck below it (looks like ":"). Taken as an ink speck.
- 31.1 opening ornament: printed as a compact ༄༅ swirl, then ༔, a wide blank, then ༔. Written ༄༅༔ ༔.
- 31.5 ཕྲལ་དྭངས and 32.3 བཙམ: no tsheg can be seen between ཕྲ and ལ, or between བ and ཙ. Kept as in the witness
  (see the misprints below).

## Suspected misprints (kept as printed)

1. 32.3 འབྲུག་སྟོང་དུས་གཅིག་ལ་**འདིར**་བཙམ་དུ: the letters are clear (འ + དི + ར). The sense calls for **ལྡིར**
   ("roar": "like a thousand thunderclaps roaring at once"), the same verb as ལྡིར་ཆེ་བ just before. The other
   recension has ལྡིར་བ་ཙམ. Certainty is fairly high. Proposed: `# fix: འདིར་བཙམ => ལྡིར་བ་ཙམ`, a misprint
   (rule 5b) plus the tsheg, since བཙམ as written is not a word.
2. 31.3 དོན་ཆེན་འགག་ལ་**ཐུགས**་པའི་དུས་ཚོད: the set phrase is འགག་ལ་ཐུག་པ ("reaching the crucial point"), and the
   other recension has ཐུག་པའི. ཐུགས ("mind", honorific) makes no sense here. Proposed: `# fix: ཐུགས་པའི => ཐུག་པའི`.
   Moderate certainty: the image agrees with the witness on ཐུགས, so this is the print's reading.
3. 31.5 སྣང་བ་**ཕྲལ**་དྭངས་པ: the sense is ཕྲ་ལ་དྭངས་པ ("subtle and clear"), which the other recension has. A tsheg is
   missing, or merged, between ཕྲ and ལ. Proposed: `# fix: ཕྲལ => ཕྲ་ལ`.
4. Possible, but not proposed: 32.3 རང་སྒྲ་**སྒྲ་དག**་ལ་ལྡིར་ཆེ་བ. Both སྒྲ stacks are certain (×6) and ད has no
   ra-btags. The other recension has རང་སྒྲ་དྲག་ལ ("loud"). This looks like a dittography plus དག for དྲག, but the
   sense does not allow only one correction, so the print is followed and a note is enough.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: 30.3 ཁྱོད་ཅིག་པོ (for གཅིག་པུ); 32.1 ཉམས་ང་བ (for ཉམ་ང); 32.3 དི་རི་རི
(the other recension has ལྡི་རི་རི; this is onomatopoeia); 32.4 རྡོས་བྱས (for གདོས་བཅས, "made of coarse matter"); 32.1 སོས་ཁ
(for སོས་ཀ); 30.1 ངོ་སྤྲད་བ.

## `# fix:` lines needed

```
# fix: གྶི => གིས
# fix: ནིའགྲོ => ནི་འགྲོ
# fix: དངངྶ => དངངས
# fix: པའིགནད => པའི་གནད
# fix: འཇིགསཤིག => འཇིགས་ཤིག
```
plus the misprint fixes proposed above (འདིར་བཙམ => ལྡིར་བ་ཙམ; ཐུགས་པའི => ཐུག་པའི; ཕྲལ => ཕྲ་ལ), if the
coordinator accepts them.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- 30.3: print འཇིག་རྟེན་འདི་ནས་ནི་འགྲོ ("goes from this world"); other recension འདི་ནས་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་འགྲོ ("goes from this
  world to the beyond"). Slight difference.
- 30.3: print ཁྱོད་ཅིག་པོ་ནི་མ་ཡིན; other recension ཁྱོད་གཅིག་པུ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ. Same sense.
- 30.4: print ཆགས་པ་དང་ཞེན་པ་བྱས་ཀྱང་སྡོད་དབང་ནི་མེད ("**even if** you cling, you have no power to stay"); other
  recension བྱས་ཅིང ("clinging, …"). The print makes it concessive.
- 30.5: print དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་དྲན་པར; other recension རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པར. Same sense.
- 31.1: print ཆོས་ཉིད་བར་དོ་ཤར་དུས; other recension འཆར་དུས. Same sense.
- 31.2: print གང་སྣང་རང་ཤར་རིག་པར་ངོ་ཤེས་བྱ ("whatever appears, self-arisen, I shall recognise as rig pa"); other
  recension གང་ཤར་རང་སྣང་…ངོ་ཤེས་འཇུག ("whatever arises, as self-appearance…, I shall enter recognition"). The terms
  are swapped and the verb differs.
- 31.4: print ཇི་ལྟར་ཤར་ཡང; other recension ཅི་ཤར་ཡང. Same sense. Print གནད་ཡོད་པས་མ་བརྗེད་ཅིག ("since it is the key
  point, do not forget"); other recension ཡོད་པ་མ་བརྗེད ("do not forget that it is the key point"). Slight difference.
- 32.1: print རང་བཞིན་བཀྲག་གསལ་ལ ("brilliant and clear"); other recension བཀྲག་ལ. The print adds གསལ.
- 32.3: print ཆོས་ཉིད་ཀྱི་རང་སྒྲ་སྒྲ་དག་ལ vs other recension རང་སྒྲ་དྲག་ལ ("loud"); see misprint 4.
- 32.4: print ཡིད་ཀྱི་ལུས་བྱ་བ་གཅིག་ཡོད་ཀྱིས; other recension ལུས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཞིག་ཡོད་ཀྱི. Same sense.
- 32.5: print མི་འོང; other recension མི་ཡོང. Same sense.
